### Also covered by

Awodey, *Category Theory* (2nd ed.), §8.1 (Set-valued functor categories),
printed page 192 (PDF page 201), item
`awodey:8.1:construction-evaluation-functor` — for each object `C` there is a
functor `ev_C : Sets^(C^op) ⟶ Sets` sending a set-valued functor `P` to the set
`P C` and a natural transformation `α : P → Q` to its component
`α_C : P C → Q C`, functoriality being exactly the componentwise definition of
identity and vertical composition of natural transformations. Same obligation
as the evaluation functor on a functor category; Awodey states it for
`Sets^(C^op)` but notes it works for any codomain.

Donor surfaced by the Awodey chapter-8 audit and worth reusing:
`Theory/Lawvere/Sets.v:83` already writes exactly this functor, but only at one
fixed object of one particular Lawvere theory — `ev1 : Models T Sets ⟶ Sets`
with object action `M ↦ M (law_of_nat 1)` and arrow action `τ ↦ τ` at that
object — over `Models T Sets`, a full subcategory of a functor category
(`Theory/Lawvere/Model.v:77`), with the functor laws discharged as
"componentwise instances of the laws of the functor category"
(`Theory/Lawvere/Sets.v:79-81`). The general `ev_C : [C,D] ⟶ D` should
generalise it, and `ev1` should then be re-expressed through it rather than
left as a parallel definition.

Awodey's section adds no obligation beyond this issue's existing scope.

### Also covered by

Awodey, *Category Theory* (2nd ed.), §8.1 (Set-valued functor categories),
printed page 192 (PDF page 201), item `awodey:8.1:example-graphs` — with `Γ` the
two-object category carrying a parallel pair of non-identity arrows `1 ⇉ 0`, a
functor `G : Γ ⟶ Sets` is exactly a directed multigraph (an edge set, a vertex
set, and source and target functions) and a natural transformation is exactly a
graph homomorphism, so `Sets^Γ` *is* the category of graphs. Awodey uses this as
the motivating reading of any `Sets^C` as a category of structured sets. Same
obligation as the functor-category presentation of directed graphs already filed
here from §7.7; no new formalizable aspect, so this is a citation only.

State of the two sides in-tree, for whoever picks this up: the shape exists as
`Instance/Parallel.v:80` (`Parallel`), and that file already states the
identification in prose at `:152-161` (citing nLab/Wikipedia "quiver") and
exhibits one worked example, `Presheaf_Graph : Parallel^op ⟶ Sets` at `:166`
(vertices `nat`, edges `nat * nat`, the two non-identity arrows going to `fst`
and `snd`). The other side is `Construction/Free/Quiver.v:358`
(`QuiverCategory`) with `:205` (`QuiverHomomorphism`). Three obstructions block
a definitional identification and should be addressed explicitly: (i)
`Construction/Free/Quiver.v:54`'s `Quiver` fibres edges over endpoint pairs
(`edges : nodes → nodes → uedges`) whereas a `Γ`-diagram supplies one global
edge setoid plus two maps; (ii) `QuiverHomomorphismEquivalence`
(`Construction/Free/Quiver.v:219`) compares node maps by strict equality with
transports, while morphisms of `[Parallel, Sets]` are compared componentwise by
`≈`; (iii) the converse of `APair` (`Instance/Parallel.v:129`) — that every
functor out of `Parallel` arises from a parallel pair — is not proved.

### Also covered by

Awodey, *Category Theory* (2nd ed.), §8.2 (The Yoneda embedding), printed page
194 (PDF page 203), item `awodey:8.2:def-embedding` — declared in running prose:
a functor is an *embedding* when it is full, faithful **and injective on
objects**. Same object-level obligation as the injectivity conditions filed
here from §7.1; Awodey additionally bundles the three conditions into a single
named notion, which the library has no counterpart for
(`rg 'Class Embedding|is_embedding|injective on objects'` — 0 hits; every
in-tree occurrence of "Embedding" is `Yoneda_Embedding` /
`Covariant_Yoneda_Embedding` / `Yoneda_Embedding'`, all of which assert
hom-setoid bijections and say nothing about objects).

What this section adds beyond the injectivity predicates themselves:

- [ ] (from Awodey §8.2) The bundled notion `Embedding F := Full F ∧ Faithful F ∧
      InjectiveOnObjects F`, with `Theory/Functor.v:331` (`Full`) and `:342`
      (`Faithful`) as the first two conjuncts, plus the elementary consequences
      (an embedding is injective on arrows; the composite of embeddings is an
      embedding) — so that later results can say "is an embedding" rather than
      restating three conditions.

### Also covered by

Awodey, *Category Theory* (2nd ed.), §8.3 (The Yoneda lemma), closing prose of
the section, printed page 199 (PDF page 208), item
`awodey:8.3:prop-yoneda-injective-objects` — the claim that the Yoneda embedding
is *injective on objects*, so that together with Theorem 8.3 it is an embedding
in the sense of §8.2. Same object-level obligation as the injectivity conditions
filed here from §7.1, instantiated at `y`.

Two honest caveats for whoever implements it. (1) The book's printed argument
switches variable names mid-sentence (it opens with objects `A, B` and then
argues with `C, D`); the intended statement is `y A = y B → A = B`. (2) The
library systematically avoids object-level equality
(`Instance/Cat.v:63` records this as the reason `Cat` is built as it is), and
the nearby in-tree fact — `Theory/Functor.v:355`
`FullyFaithful : ∀ x y, F x ≅ F y → x ≅ y`, which at `F = y` gives
`y A ≅ y B → A ≅ B` — is *reflection of isomorphisms*, a different and
foundations-independent claim already covered by the Yoneda full-and-faithful
material. So this is genuinely additional, and genuinely low priority.

- [ ] (from Awodey §8.3) `InjectiveOnObjects (Curried_CoHom C)`, i.e.
      `y A = y B → A = B`, stated over whatever object-equality discipline this
      issue settles on, with the header recording why the library otherwise
      avoids the notion.

### Also covered by

Awodey, *Category Theory* (2nd ed.), §8.2 (The Yoneda embedding), printed pages
194–195 (PDF pages 203–204), item `awodey:8.2:construction-cayley` — the book
recalls the Cayley representation (a group `G` embeds in `Aut(|G|) ⊆ |G|^|G|` by
left translation `g ↦ g·(−)`, with `(g·h)~ = g~ ∘ h~`; likewise any monoid `M`
into `End(|M|)`) and then uses it as the prototype for Yoneda. Same obligation
as Cayley's theorem as filed from §1.5.

What §8.2 adds is the *failure* half and its repair, which is the whole point of
the recap and which no filed issue covers:

- [ ] (from Awodey §8.2) The representation is faithful but **not full**:
      exhibit a self-map of the underlying set of a group that is not a left
      translation (a two-element group suffices), so that non-fullness is
      proved, not merely remarked.
- [ ] (from Awodey §8.2) Fullness is recovered by restricting to
      **right-equivariant** maps: if `α(x·g) = α(x)·g` for all `g` then `α` is a
      left translation. In-tree this is the one-object instance of
      `Functor/Hom.v:96`'s `Yoneda_Full` (whose `prefmap` is evaluation at the
      identity, `fun c d f => f c id`) and of `Functor/Hom/Yoneda.v:253`'s
      `Covariant_Yoneda_Embedding`; state the monoid/group case and connect it to
      the general lemma rather than leaving the two unrelated.
- [ ] (from Awodey §8.2) Connect `Construction/Cayley.v:114`, whose hom type
      *builds in* the equivariance law (`∀ r k, f r k ≈ k ∘ f _ id`) as a field,
      to the general derivation — the library currently assumes exactly what the
      book proves.
- [ ] (library defect found while auditing this item) `Construction/Cayley.v`'s
      header at `:39-41` claims "the embedding is (split) faithful:
      `From_Cayley (To_Cayley f) ≈ f`", but no such lemma exists anywhere in the
      file; the round trip is used only implicitly inside `Cayley_Right` /
      `Cayley_Left`, which are stated with Leibniz `=` under a strict-`id_left`
      hypothesis. Either prove the stated round trip with `≈`, or correct the
      header to what the file establishes.

### Also covered by

Awodey, *Category Theory* (2nd ed.), §8.3 (The Yoneda lemma), Lemma 8.2, printed
pages 195–199 (PDF pages 204–208), item `awodey:8.3:lem2` — for a locally small
`C`, every object `C` and every presheaf `F`, an isomorphism
`Hom_{Sets^(C^op)}(y C, F) ≅ F C`, **natural in both `F` and `C`**: forward
`ϑ ↦ ϑ_C(1_C)`, inverse `a ↦ ϑ_a` with `(ϑ_a)_{C'}(h) = F(h)(a)`; naturality in
`F` is the square relating `Hom(y C, ϑ)` to the component `ϑ_C`, and naturality
in `C` the square relating `Hom(y h, F)` to `F h`. Same obligation as the
naturality of the Yoneda isomorphism in both variables.

The bijection itself is in-tree at full strength and matches the book's two maps
verbatim — `Functor/Hom/Yoneda.v:133`
`Yoneda_Lemma (C : Category) (F : C^op ⟶ Sets) : ∀ A : C, Presheaves [Hom ─,A] F ≅ F A`
with `to := fun x => transform[x] A id` and
`from := fun y => the transformation phi ↦ fmap[F] phi y`, the two round trips
discharged at `:166-171` (by `fmap_id`) and `:172-179` (by naturality), exactly
Awodey's proof. What is missing is only naturality: the statement is a bare
`∀ A` product with `F` a fixed section parameter.

What this section adds beyond the covariant statement:

- [ ] (from Awodey §8.3) The **contravariant/presheaf orientation**: naturality
      in both arguments for `Functor/Hom/Yoneda.v:133`'s `Yoneda_Lemma`
      (`Presheaves [Hom ─,A] F ≅ F A`), not only for
      `Covariant_Yoneda_Lemma` (`:182`). The two are separate constants in this
      library, so the presheaf orientation Awodey uses needs its own statement;
      naturality in `F` in particular requires organising both sides as functors
      `[C^op, Sets] ⟶ Sets`, which no file does.
- [ ] (library defect found while auditing this item) `Functor/Hom/Yoneda.v:22`
      advertises in the file header `Nat([Hom ─,A], F) ≅ F A, natural in both A
      and F` — a claim the file does not deliver. Fix the header when the
      naturality statements land (or soften it immediately if this issue lands
      only the covariant half).

### Also covered by

Awodey, *Category Theory* (2nd ed.), §8.3 (The Yoneda lemma), Remark 8.4,
printed page 199 (PDF page 208), item `awodey:8.3:remark4` — the size trichotomy
for Yoneda: (i) if `C` is small then `Sets^(C^op)` is locally small, so
`Hom(y C, P)` is a set for every presheaf `P`; (ii) if `C` is only locally small
then `Sets^(C^op)` need not be locally small, yet the Yoneda lemma still
guarantees that `Hom(y C, P) ≅ P C` is a set; (iii) if `C` is not locally small
then `y` is not even definable. Same smallness/foundations obligation filed here
from §1.8 and MacLane §I.6.

In-tree the discipline is enforced but unstatable: `Theory/Category.v:111-116`
gives every category `hom : obj → obj → Type@{h}` with a `Setoid` on each
hom-set, so case (iii) cannot arise and local smallness is built into the class;
`rg 'Class Small|IsSmall|LocallySmall'` returns 0 hits, and
`Theory/Lawvere/Sets.v:44` records in-tree that "the library has no smallness
machinery". Note also that `Functor/Hom.v` and `Functor/Hom/Yoneda.v` carry no
explicit `Universe` declarations at all, so the constraints doing the work are
inferred and unreadable as the book's remark.

What this section adds:

- [ ] (from Awodey §8.3) The Yoneda-specific size statements, once smallness
      vocabulary exists: `C` small ⇒ `[C^op, Sets]` locally small; and case (ii),
      that `Hom(y C, P)` is a set even when `[C^op, Sets]` is not locally small.
      The second is worth stating explicitly because the in-tree
      `Yoneda_Lemma` currently *presupposes* it — both sides of its `≅` must
      already be `Sets`-objects for the statement to typecheck (via the
      `Coercion Curried_Hom` at `Functor/Hom.v:78`) — rather than concluding it.

### Also covered by

Awodey, *Category Theory* (2nd ed.), §8.5 (Limits in categories of diagrams),
Proposition 8.7, printed pages 201–202 (PDF pages 210–211), item
`awodey:8.5:prop7` — for any locally small `C`, `Sets^(C^op)` is complete and
every evaluation functor `ev_C : Sets^(C^op) ⟶ Sets` preserves **all** limits,
the limit being *defined* pointwise by `(lim_i F_i)(C) = lim_i (F_i C)` (display
(8.2)) and shown to be one by Yoneda plus continuity of representables. Same
obligation as pointwise limits in a functor category and their preservation by
evaluation.

In-tree only the binary-product shape exists: `Instance/Fun/Cartesian.v:111`
(`Functor_Category_Cartesian`), whose product is literally `fun c => F c × G c`
with the universal property discharged componentwise. There is no `Complete`
inhabitant anywhere in the tree (`@Complete` occurs only as a hypothesis, in
`Construction/Comma/Limit.v`, `Adjunction/GAFT.v`, `Adjunction/SAFT.v`), no
`Instance/Fun/Limit.v`, and no functor `[C,D] ⟶ D`. The general principle is
recorded only as a header comment at `Instance/Fun.v:101-106`.

What this section adds:

- [ ] (from Awodey §8.5) The concrete corollary `Complete [C^op, Sets]` — i.e.
      completeness of presheaf categories — assembled from the general pointwise
      theorem and a `Complete Sets` witness (#254). The library today has no
      `Complete` inhabitant at all, so the base case must be landed or named as
      a blocker rather than assumed.

### Also covered by

Awodey, *Category Theory* (2nd ed.), §8.6 (Colimits in categories of diagrams),
Proposition 8.10, printed pages 203–205 (PDF pages 212–214), item
`awodey:8.6:prop10` — every presheaf on a small category is a colimit of
representables: with `J` the category of elements of `P` and `A : J ⟶ C` the
projection, `colim_J (y ∘ A) ≅ P`, the cocone component at `(x, C)` being the
arrow `y C → P` that Yoneda associates with `x ∈ P(C)`. Same obligation as the
density theorem filed here; Awodey states it in the contravariant (presheaf)
orientation.

Donors surfaced by the chapter-8 audit, both stating the same content in
**coend** form: `Construction/Profunctor/Laws.v:236`
`prof_unit_left_iso : prof_compose prof_id P ≅[Fun] P` is a genuine isomorphism
in the functor category (naturality from `lu_natural_form` at `:217`), which at
`D = 1` reads `∫^m C(−,m) × P(m) ≅ P`; and `Theory/Coend/Yoneda.v:174`
`coyoneda_reduction : coend_obj (SetsCoend YoI) ≅[Sets] F c` gives the same
reduction pointwise and funext-free. Neither is connected to
`Structure/Limit.v`'s `Colimit`: there is no in-tree lemma identifying a coend
with a colimit (`rg 'Colimit' Structure/Coend.v Structure/End.v Instance/Sets/Coend.v`
— 0 hits), so "colimit of representables" as opposed to "coend of
representables" still has to be stated. Whoever closes this issue should decide
explicitly whether to prove the colimit form directly (Awodey's route) or to
build the coend-is-a-colimit bridge and transport.

### Also covered by

Awodey, *Category Theory* (2nd ed.), §8.6 (Colimits in categories of diagrams),
developed inside the proof of Proposition 8.10 and illustrated by Figure 8.1,
printed pages 203–205 (PDF pages 212–214), item
`awodey:8.6:construction-category-of-elements` — for a presheaf `P : C^op ⟶ Sets`
the category of elements has objects the pairs `(x, C)` with `x ∈ P(C)` and
arrows `h : (x',C') → (x,C)` the arrows `h : C' → C` of `C` with `P(h)(x) = x'`,
identities and composition inherited from `C`; it is small when `C` is, and the
projection functor sends `(x,C) ↦ C` and an arrow to its underlying `h`. Same
obligation as the category of elements of a set-valued functor.

Route note from the chapter-8 audit, worth recording in the implementing PR: the
**comma** route is a zero-content instantiation and is probably the cheapest
path — `Construction/Comma.v:127` (`Comma`) at `S :=` the constant singleton
functor `1 ⟶ Sets` and `T := P` yields both the category and its projection
(`Construction/Comma.v:196,204`, `comma_proj1`/`comma_proj2`) with no new
mathematics. The Grothendieck route is *not* available as-is: it consumes an
`IndexedCat` (`Construction/Indexed.v`) or a strict functor into `Cat`
(`Construction/Grothendieck/Strict.v:225`), and there is no discretisation
`Sets ⟶ Cat` in the tree (`Instance/Discrete.v:52` only provides a functor *out*
of a discrete category). `Construction/Grothendieck.v:108` names el(F) in a
header comment as the fibres-are-sets restriction, which is a mathematical
aside, not an in-tree definition.

### Also covered by

Awodey, *Category Theory* (2nd ed.), §8.7 (Exponentials in categories of
diagrams), printed pages 207–208 (PDF pages 216–217), item
`awodey:8.7:remark-pointwise-exponential-fails` — the text poses and answers
negatively the naive attempt to define exponentials of presheaves objectwise by
`Q^P(C) := Q(C)^(P(C))`: the assignment is not functorial (nothing makes it
contravariant in `C`), which is precisely why the Yoneda-derived formula of
display (8.5) is adopted instead. Same family of negative results about
exponentials in functor categories as the counterexample filed here from
MacLane §IV.6, and one countermodel file can reasonably host both.

Nothing in-tree touches it: `rg -i 'not functorial'` and `rg -i 'objectwise
exponential'` return 0 hits, and `Instance/Fun.v:101-106` is honest — it
attributes the positive cartesian-closure fact to nLab and says only the
cartesian case is instantiated. Note that the library does carry comparable
no-go disclosures (the 2-cocycle countermodel in `Theory/Displayed.v`, the
Joyal no-go note in `Structure/Monoidal/StarAutonomous.v`), so this is a genuine
gap rather than a stylistic exclusion.

What this section adds:

- [ ] (from Awodey §8.7) The specific no-go: the objectwise assignment
      `c ↦ Q(c)^(P(c))` carries no contravariant action, exhibited by a
      countermodel (a two-object `C` suffices) rather than asserted — and, once
      the presheaf exponential lands, a header note in the closed-structure file
      recording why the pointwise formula is not used.

### Also covered by

Awodey, *Category Theory* (2nd ed.), §8.8 (Topoi), Proposition 8.17, printed
pages 210–211 (PDF pages 219–220), item `awodey:8.8:prop17` — for any small `C`
the diagram category `Sets^(C^op)` is a topos: finite limits and exponentials
come from the preceding sections, and the classifier is built from sieves, with
`Ω(C)` the set of sieves on `C`, restriction `h*(S) = {g : h ∘ g ∈ S}`,
`t : 1 → Ω` the total sieve, and the classifying map of `U ↣ E` given at `C` by
`u_C(e) = {f : D → C : f*(e) ∈ U(D)}`. Same obligation as presheaf categories
being elementary toposes.

Current in-tree state, so the scope is not overestimated: exactly **one** of the
five `ElementaryTopos` fields (`Structure/Topos.v:112`) is available for a
functor category — `Instance/Fun/Cartesian.v:111` gives binary products
pointwise — and that fragment is generic functor-category content, not
distinctive to this proposition. There is no `@Terminal (@Fun _ _)`, no
`HasPullbacks` for a functor category (the only instance in the tree is
`Instance/FinSet/Classifier.v:264`), no `@Closed (@Fun _ _)`, and no classifier;
the only `ElementaryTopos` inhabitant anywhere is `Instance/FinSet/Topos.v:38`.
The two missing components are separately catalogued: the classifier by #403,
and the cartesian-closure component by the Awodey §8.7 issue covering
`awodey:8.7:def-presheaf-exponential`.

### Also covered by

Awodey, *Category Theory* (2nd ed.), §8.8 (Topoi), defined in running prose
inside the proof of Proposition 8.17, printed page 210 (PDF page 219), item
`awodey:8.8:def-sieve` — a sieve on an object `C` is a set `S` of arrows with
codomain `C` closed under precomposition (`f ∈ S` and `g` composable ⇒
`f ∘ g ∈ S`), glossed by the book as the generalisation of a lower
(downward-closed) set in a poset. Same obligation as the sieve machinery this
issue's classifier construction is built from.

There is no sieve anywhere in the tree: `rg -in 'sieve|crible'` returns exactly
two lines, both comments (`Theory/Sheaf.v:80`, `Construction/Localization.v:101`),
and 0 hits for `cosieve`/`subpresheaf`. Note that `Theory/Sheaf.v:159`'s
`Class Site` is *not* a donor: it encodes a coverage by vector-indexed covering
families (`covering_family (u : C) := sigT (Vector.t (∃ uᵢ, uᵢ ~> u))`, `:162`,
with a single chosen family per object) and carries no
closure-under-precomposition condition at all.

What this section adds:

- [ ] (from Awodey §8.8) A standalone, exported `Sieve` definition (the set of
      arrows into an object, closed under precomposition, as a subobject of the
      representable presheaf) rather than an inlined construction inside the
      classifier proof — sieves are reused by the sheaf/site development
      (`Theory/Sheaf.v`) and by orthogonal localization
      (`Construction/Localization.v:101`), and the poset special case is the
      lower-set construction filed for Awodey §8.2.

### Also covered by

Awodey, *Category Theory* (2nd ed.), §8.8 (Topoi), constructed inside the proof
of Proposition 8.17, printed pages 210–211 (PDF pages 219–220), item
`awodey:8.8:construction-omega-sieves` — the presheaf `Ω : C^op ⟶ Sets` sending
an object to its set of sieves and an arrow `h : D → C` to the restriction
`h*(S) = {g : h ∘ g ∈ S}`, its global point `t : 1 → Ω` picking the total sieve
("true") at each object, and the classifying transformation of a subpresheaf
`U ↣ E` given by `u_C(e) = {f : D → C : f*(e) ∈ U(D)}`. This is exactly the
construction this issue exists to formalize; Awodey leaves the verification that
`u` is the unique classifying morphism to the reader, so the uniqueness clause
is real work.

No part of it is in-tree: `rg 'Omega_presheaf|Sieves|sieve_presheaf|truth_presheaf'`
— 0 hits; the only `SubobjectClassifier` instance in the tree is
`Instance/FinSet/Classifier.v:354`, and `Instance/Sets/Classifier.v:21-45`
deliberately supplies cross-universe theorems instead of an instance. There is
not even a `Terminal` instance for a functor category, so the domain `1` of
`t : 1 ⟹ Ω` must be built first (`ls Instance/Fun/` shows `Cartesian.v` as the
sole satellite).

### Also covered by

Awodey, *Category Theory* (2nd ed.), §8.8 (Topoi), the closure remark stated
without proof immediately after Definition 8.16, printed page 210 (PDF page
219), item `awodey:8.8:remark-topos-properties` — every topos has all finite
colimits (and, in the same breath, every slice of a topos is again a topos).
Same obligation as the finite-cocompleteness of an elementary topos filed here;
Awodey refers the reader to Mac Lane–Moerdijk, Johnstone and McLarty.

In-tree nothing derives colimit structure from `Structure/Topos.v:112`'s
`ElementaryTopos`: `rg 'topos' | rg -i 'colimit|coproduct|cocomplete|initial'`
finds a single hit, `Structure/Topos.v:91`, inside the Giraud-theorem paragraph
of the header essay, and `Cocomplete` (`Structure/Complete.v:119`) has no
inhabitant at all. The class has exactly one inhabitant tree-wide,

The remark's other half — the fundamental theorem of topos theory, that every

### Also covered by

Awodey, *Category Theory* (2nd ed.), §8.8 (Topoi), Remark 8.18, printed page 211
(PDF page 220), item `awodey:8.8:remark18` — because subobjects `U ↣ E`
correspond to arrows `u : E → Ω`, the classifier behaves as an object of truth
values with `t` as "true", `u` as a propositional function and `U` as its
extension; the classifying pullback then yields the **membership criterion**: a
generalized element `x : X → E` lies in `U` (factors through `U ↣ E`) if and
only if `u ∘ x = true`, so `U = {x ∈ E : u x = true}` in the generalized-element
notation of §5.1. Same obligation as local membership of generalized elements,
now in its subobject-classifier form.

In-tree the content is present but never packaged: `char_pullback`
(`Structure/SubobjectClassifier.v:52`) is a field of the classifier class whose
universal property (`IsPullback`, `Theory/Morphisms/Stability.v:53`) says
exactly that any `z` with `char m ∘ z ≈ truth ∘ one` factors uniquely through
`m` — but no lemma states the equivalence, and
`rg -i 'factors through|factor_through|sub_factor'` over `Theory/Subobject*.v`
finds only prose comments at `Theory/Subobject.v:55,88`. The classification
bijection itself is `classifier_classifies` (`:187`) and the power object is
`Pow a := Ω ^ a` with `relations_iso` (`Structure/Topos.v:146`).

What this section adds:

- [ ] (from Awodey §8.8) The membership criterion as a named lemma in
      classifier form: `(∃ k, m ∘ k ≈ z) ↔ char m M ∘ z ≈ truth ∘ one` for a
      mono `m` and a generalized element `z`, linking §5.1's local membership to
      `Structure/SubobjectClassifier.v`'s `char_pullback` (from which it is
      recoverable but currently never extracted).

### Also covered by

Awodey, *Category Theory* (2nd ed.), §8.8 (Topoi), Remark 8.18, printed page 211
(PDF page 220), item `awodey:8.8:remark18` — the remark records (as a forward
reference to the book's §9.5) that a topos models the first-order quantifiers as
adjoints to pullback, and that combining cartesian closure with the classifier
interprets higher-order logic, with `Ω^E` serving as the power object `P(E)`.
Same obligation as quantifiers-as-adjoints-to-substitution filed here, raised
from the powerset preorder to an arbitrary topos.

In-tree the base-change functors exist but their adjunction does not:
`Construction/Slice/Pullback.v:50` defines `Bang_Functor f` (`Σ_f`) and `:67`
`Star_Functor f` (`f*`), while the adjunction itself is a commented-out stub —
lines 114–125 are `(* Program Definition Production … *)` and
`(* Program Definition Base_Functor_Adjunction … *)`, with the file header
noting an orientation erratum. There is no `Π_f`, so no universal quantifier.
The power-object half of the remark *is* in-tree: `Structure/Topos.v:129`
(`Pow a := Ω ^ a`) with `:146` `relations_iso : SubObj (a × b) ≅ (a ~> Pow b)`.
The higher-order-logic clause (an internal language / Mitchell–Bénabou
interpretation) has no in-tree counterpart and is closest to #695.

What this section adds:

- [ ] (from Awodey §8.8) The topos-level form of the correspondence: the
      adjoint triple `Σ_f ⊣ f* ⊣ Π_f` on subobject lattices of an elementary
      topos (rather than on powerset preorders), giving existential and
      universal quantification along an arbitrary arrow, over
      `Theory/Subobject/Functor.v:180`'s `Sub : C^op ⟶ Sets` and the classifier.
